sections.h2: A residential painting contractor for the whole house, not one wall at a time
body: Most homeowners call us about one thing: the faded west wall, the scuffed hallway, the kitchen that still has builder-beige walls. By the time we finish the walkthrough, the conversation is usually about the house as a whole. That is what residential painting means to us: a plan that covers walls, ceilings, trim, doors, siding, and fascia in the right order, with one crew lead accountable for all of it.

From our home base in Newberry, we serve as a residential painting contractor in North Central Florida for homeowners in five counties: Alachua, Marion, Levy, Columbia, and Gilchrist. We are locally owned, and the painters standing in your yard are our employees; a signed house estimate never gets passed down the line to some other outfit.

Typical residential projects look like this: a family preparing a Newberry ranch house for sale who needs neutral walls and fresh trim inside and a clean exterior; a couple in an older Gainesville home whose wood siding is peeling on the sunny side; new owners in Ocala who want every room repainted before the furniture arrives. Each one gets the same walkthrough, the same written scope, and the same crew lead from start to finish.

sections.h2: What we look at before quoting a house
body: A house repaint is really a repair job that ends in paint. The person who tours your home is a crew lead rather than a sales rep, and that visit is hands-on: tape measure on every wall and elevation, photos of each problem spot, and a moisture meter pressed against any wood or stucco that seems off. We push on fascia and soffit boards, check the bottom courses of siding where splash-back sits, look at window sills and door thresholds, and note interior issues like nail pops, ceiling stains, and cracked corner bead.

Those notes become line items. If a run of fascia is soft, the estimate says it gets replaced, not painted over. If a bathroom ceiling has a water stain, it gets a stain-blocking primer before the topcoat. Spotting this before we quote is the difference between a repaint that lasts and one that starts failing in two years. Curious what a soft board looks like before it fails? We wrote up the warning signs in a post about rot hiding behind house siding.
bullets: Exterior: siding, stucco, trim, fascia, soffit, doors, shutters, and garage doors
Interior: walls, ceilings, trim, doors, built-ins, and stair rails
Repairs: rot replacement, drywall patching, caulking, and nail pops
Specialty add-ons: cabinets, decks, fences, and pressure washing

sections.h2: Interior or exterior first? How we sequence a full home
body: If you are doing both, the exterior usually goes first when the calendar allows, because our best outdoor season runs from October through May. Indoor rooms ignore the weather entirely, which makes them the natural job for the summer stretch when afternoon storms cut exterior days short. Some families split the house across two seasons to spread the cost; because each room and elevation carries a separate figure on the itemized estimate, that split takes no rework.

On the inside, see our interior painting service for how we handle masking, drywall, and sheen. On the outside, our exterior house painting page covers washing, caulking, and coating systems for stucco and siding. Kitchen cabinets are their own trade, and we handle them through cabinet painting and refinishing on a separate schedule so the kitchen is not out of service longer than it needs to be.

sections.h2: Products, coats, and the finish you live with
body: Paint for a whole house comes from the premium Sherwin-Williams and Benjamin Moore ranges, and your estimate spells out which line goes where. Around a typical North Central Florida home, the siding and trim take a 100% acrylic, any stucco showing hairline movement gets an elastomeric, front doors and porch railings get a waterborne urethane enamel, and the bedrooms and living areas get low-VOC wall paint. Every surface in the house gets at least two full coats; a dramatic color swap or a thirsty, porous substrate earns a third.

Stuck between swatches for the living room and the shutters? Book a color consultation so the palette is decided before a single gallon is ordered. Want to keep a shade you already love? Bring a paint chip, pull a door off its hinges, or dig out the old can from the garage, and we will match it with full-size drawdowns.
Eco-conscious, low-odor products can go in any room you like, and they suit for nurseries, bedrooms, and homes with family members who are sensitive to paint odor.

sections.h2: Staying in the house during your repaint
body: Nobody has to pack a suitcase. The crew shifts and covers your furniture themselves and moves through the house one room at a time, leaving the kitchen and at least one bathroom usable. Plan on roughly one day per room indoors, and somewhere between three days and two weeks for an entire interior, with size and repair work setting the pace. Outside, the full house body and trim generally need three to seven working days, not counting washing and dry time.

On the last day the crew lead tours every room and elevation with you, and the punch list gets your signature only after each item you flag has been corrected. You keep labelled cans for touch-ups, plus a written workmanship warranty that runs as long as 10 years on the outside of the house and stacks on the paint maker's own coverage. If you live in one of the two biggest markets we cover, see the Gainesville residential painting and Ocala residential painting pages.

faqs.q: Should I paint the inside and outside of my house at the same time?
faqs.a: You can, and one crew can handle both. A popular plan is siding and trim between October and May, when the air is drier and cooler, then the inside rooms in July or August when the weather no longer matters. With every room and elevation priced on its own, splitting the job is painless.

faqs.q: What does a residential painting estimate include?
faqs.a: Your house quote is itemized: which surfaces are in and which are out, every prep and repair task, the primer and finish products named outright, how many coats each area receives, and the dates. Expect it in your inbox about one business day after the crew lead's visit, and know that no line can be added afterward unless you sign off in writing.

faqs.q: Do I have to move out while my house is being painted?
faqs.a: No. Families keep living at home throughout; the painters handle furniture and coverings and finish one space before opening up the next. Low-VOC paint in bedrooms and common rooms keeps the smell manageable.
Call today and a crew lead can typically be at your house inside 48 hours. Once you accept the quote, painting on most homes begins one to three weeks later.
